title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent
plain: The engine speed (RPM) signal the transmission computer relies on keeps dropping in and out.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Erratic or harsh shifting
Engine may stumble or stall if the crankshaft signal drops

causes.name: Loose or corroded connector at the crankshaft position sensor
Failing crankshaft position sensor
Chafed wiring between the engine and transmission computers

checks: Wiggle-test the crankshaft sensor connector and wiring with the engine running
Check for crankshaft sensor or network codes
fix: Usually a connector or wiring repair, or a new crankshaft position sensor.

title: Gear 6 Incorrect Ratio
plain: The computer compared the speeds going into and out of the transmission and found they don't match what sixth gear should give, which usually means something is slipping.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Slipping or flaring RPM during or after a shift
Delayed, harsh or missing gear

causes.name: Low, burnt or wrong transmission fluid
Worn clutches or bands inside the transmission
Faulty shift solenoid or pressure control solenoid

checks: Check fluid level, color and smell (dark or burnt fluid points to internal wear)
Check for solenoid or speed sensor codes and fix those first
fix: Check and correct the fluid first. If solenoids and sensors test good, the transmission usually needs internal repair or a rebuild.

title: Stuck in Neutral
plain: The computer has found the transmission stuck in neutral, so engine power isn't reaching the wheels.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission will not shift out of (or into) the gear named in the code
Car may be stuck in limp mode or unable to move

causes.name: Faulty shift solenoid or valve body
Low fluid or low line pressure
Worn or damaged clutch inside the transmission
Shift cable or range sensor fault

checks: Check the fluid level and condition
Read all transmission codes and check solenoid operation with a scanner
Make sure the shift cable and range sensor are adjusted correctly
fix: Depends on the cause: fluid correction, solenoid or valve body repair, or internal transmission repair.
drive: No. If the transmission is stuck in neutral, the engine can't move the car, and it may lose drive without warning while moving. Get safely off the road, put it in Park with the parking brake set, and have it towed rather than trying to drive it.
test_first: Check fluid level and condition, read all transmission codes, verify shift cable and range sensor adjustment, and test solenoids and line pressure before assuming internal clutch damage.

title: Stuck in Reverse

drive: No. A transmission stuck in reverse, or engaging reverse when it shouldn't, can make the car move the wrong way. Don't drive it. Set the parking brake, shut the engine off and have it towed.
test_first: Check fluid level, read all transmission codes, verify shift cable and range sensor alignment, and test solenoid and valve body operation before any internal transmission repair.

title: Incorrect Gear Ratio
plain: The computer compared the speeds going into and out of the transmission and found they don't match any gear it expects, which usually means something is slipping.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Slipping or flaring RPM during or after a shift
Delayed, harsh or missing gear
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Low, burnt or wrong transmission fluid
Worn clutches or bands inside the transmission
Faulty shift solenoid or pressure control solenoid
Sticking valve in the valve body
Faulty input or output speed sensor

checks: Check fluid level, color and smell (dark or burnt fluid points to internal wear)
Check for solenoid or speed sensor codes and fix those first
Compare input and output speeds on a scanner in each gear
fix: Check and correct the fluid first. If solenoids and sensors test good, the transmission usually needs internal repair or a rebuild.
drive: Drive as little as possible. Slipping wears the transmission quickly and can get worse suddenly. If RPM flares, it won't go into gear, it's in limp mode or you smell burnt fluid, avoid highways and consider a tow. Short, gentle trips to a shop soon at most.
test_first: Check fluid level, color and smell, fix any solenoid or speed sensor codes first, and compare input and output speeds in each gear on a scanner before deciding on a rebuild.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit
plain: There's an electrical problem with the solenoid that locks the torque converter at cruising speed. The car still drives, but fuel economy usually drops.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Worse fuel economy
Higher RPM than normal at highway speed
Shudder at 30 to 50 mph or stalling when coming to a stop

causes.name: Faulty torque converter clutch solenoid
Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)
Low or burnt transmission fluid
Worn torque converter
Faulty brake switch signal

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Check the solenoid resistance and wiring through the transmission connector
Watch converter slip on a scanner at steady highway speed
fix: Most often a new torque converter clutch solenoid or a wiring repair; a worn converter needs the transmission removed.
drive: Usually drivable to a shop in the next few days; expect higher RPM on the highway and worse fuel economy. If the engine stalls when you stop, the car shudders badly, or it slips or overheats, limit driving and get it checked right away, as stalling in traffic is dangerous.
test_first: Check fluid level and condition, measure solenoid resistance and the wiring through the transmission connector, and confirm the computer is commanding lockup before replacing the solenoid.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
plain: The torque converter is supposed to lock up at cruising speed but it's slipping or not locking at all, so the engine revs higher than it should.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Worse fuel economy
Higher RPM than normal at highway speed
Shudder at 30 to 50 mph or stalling when coming to a stop

causes.name: Low, burnt or contaminated transmission fluid
Worn torque converter clutch
Faulty or sticking torque converter clutch solenoid
Worn valve body or seals causing low apply pressure
Engine performance problem confusing the lockup test

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Check the solenoid resistance and wiring through the transmission connector
Watch converter slip on a scanner at steady highway speed
fix: Most often a new torque converter clutch solenoid or a wiring repair; a worn converter needs the transmission removed.
examples: Frequently seen on GM trucks and SUVs with the 4L60-E automatic
drive: Usually drivable gently for now, but a slipping converter makes heat that can hurt the transmission. Avoid towing and long highway runs. If you see a transmission temperature warning, smell burnt fluid, feel heavy shudder or the engine stalls at stops, get it checked right away.
test_first: Check fluid level and condition, watch commanded versus actual converter slip at steady highway speed, and test the solenoid and apply pressure before condemning the torque converter.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Stuck On
plain: The torque converter clutch is staying locked when it should release, which can stall the engine as you come to a stop.
symptoms: Engine stalls or nearly stalls when stopping
Car bucks or shudders at low speed
Check engine light on

causes.name: Sticking torque converter clutch solenoid or valve
Wiring short keeping the solenoid powered
Debris in the valve body

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Check the solenoid resistance and wiring through the transmission connector
Watch converter slip on a scanner at steady highway speed
fix: Most often a new torque converter clutch solenoid or a wiring repair; a worn converter needs the transmission removed.
drive: Be careful. A converter that stays locked can stall the engine when you stop, leaving you with heavy steering and harder braking in traffic. If it stalls or nearly stalls, don't keep driving; have it towed or move it only a short, low-traffic distance to a shop.
test_first: Confirm with a scanner whether the converter stays locked when stopping, then check the solenoid and its wiring for a short, and the valve body for sticking or debris.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Electrical

causes.name: Faulty torque converter clutch solenoid

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Check the solenoid resistance and wiring through the transmission connector
Watch converter slip on a scanner at steady highway speed
fix: Most often a new torque converter clutch solenoid or a wiring repair; a worn converter needs the transmission removed.
drive: Usually drivable to a shop in the next few days, with higher highway RPM and worse fuel economy. If the engine stalls when you come to a stop, the car shudders hard, or the transmission slips, keep driving to a minimum and get it checked right away.
test_first: Measure the solenoid's resistance and check the circuit for opens or shorts through the transmission connector and internal harness before replacing the solenoid or computer.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Intermittent

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Check the solenoid resistance and wiring through the transmission connector
Watch converter slip on a scanner at steady highway speed
fix: Most often a new torque converter clutch solenoid or a wiring repair; a worn converter needs the transmission removed.
drive: Usually drivable with care, but lockup may come and go, causing shudder or surging. If the engine stalls when you stop, the car bucks hard or a transmission warning appears, limit driving and get it checked promptly.
test_first: Wiggle-test the connector and harness while watching the solenoid circuit on a scanner, check for corrosion or fluid in the connector, and confirm the dropout before replacing parts.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid A
plain: There's a problem with the solenoid that controls the hydraulic pressure the transmission uses to apply its clutches, which affects how firmly it shifts.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Harsh or very soft shifts
Slipping or delayed engagement
Transmission stuck in limp mode

causes.name: Faulty pressure control solenoid
Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)
Low or dirty transmission fluid
Sticking valve in the valve body
Transmission computer fault

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
Check line pressure with a gauge if shifting is harsh or soft
fix: Usually a new pressure control solenoid (on some models part of the solenoid pack or valve body) or a wiring repair.
drive: Drive gently and only as needed to get it checked soon. Wrong line pressure can make shifts slam or slip, and slipping wears clutches fast. If it's stuck in limp mode, won't engage a gear, slips or flares in RPM, avoid highways and consider a tow.
test_first: Check fluid level and condition, measure the solenoid resistance at the connector, and check line pressure with a gauge before replacing the solenoid, solenoid pack or valve body.

title: Unable to Engage Gear 5
plain: The computer commanded gear 5 but the transmission did not go into it.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission will not shift out of (or into) the gear named in the code
Car may be stuck in limp mode or unable to move

causes.name: Faulty shift solenoid or valve body
Low fluid or low line pressure
Worn or damaged clutch inside the transmission
Shift cable or range sensor fault

checks: Check the fluid level and condition
Read all transmission codes and check solenoid operation with a scanner
Make sure the shift cable and range sensor are adjusted correctly
fix: Depends on the cause: fluid correction, solenoid or valve body repair, or internal transmission repair.
